[0] everyday_reading (E): Everyday reading of a "dead-end" page is that the surfer just stops or stays there; in the model the surfer always goes somewhere, so a page with no outlinks must still have a full probability row (1/N to every page).
[1] misconception (M) -> RowsNeedNotSumToOne: wrong rule: A page with no outgoing links can have an all-zero row. Right rule: Every row must sum to 1; fill the row of a page with no outgoing links with 1/N (equally likely to go to every page).
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> RowsNeedNotSumToOne: Applies LT (test outDegree[i] == 0 before dividing; if so use 1.0/N for the whole row) unevenly: e.g. tests only on the first column, or still adds the .10/N leap term to the 1/N entries so the row sums to more than 1. (here mixing in: "A page with no outgoing links can have an all-zero row")

[0] names_the_element (N): A page with no outgoing links (outDegree 0), also called a dangling page or sink; spider traps are sets of such pages.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Transition assumes there are none; to handle them, fill the row of every page with no outgoing links with 1/N, which keeps the matrix stochastic.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): For row i: first test outDegree[i] == 0; if true every p[i][j] = 1.0/N; otherwise use .90*counts[i][j]/outDegree[i] + .10/N. The test must come before the division.
[1] output_prediction (OP): A dangling page's row is N equal entries 1/N (for N = 5, 0.20000 each), summing to 1.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): Handling one dangling entry sets p[i][j] to the double 1.0/N; counts and outDegree are unchanged.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): A dangling page is the case where the matrix formula breaks (division by outDegree 0); the 1/N row replaces it so the matrix stays stochastic.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): A guard / special-case plan: detect the zero-total case and substitute a uniform distribution so later code (random move, power method) can assume every row sums to 1.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> RowsNeedNotSumToOne: Filling with 1/N keeps the row-sum invariant; writing 1/N with int operands (0) or leaving the row as computed (NaN) breaks it, and RandomSurfer then fails.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Needed whenever the input may contain pages with no outlinks (as the real web does, e.g. spider traps); unnecessary when every page has at least one outlink, as Transition assumes.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Transition assumes no page lacks outlinks. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Input with a page that never appears as i: its row is NaN (0.0/0), and RandomSurfer's test r < sum is always false on that row, so the surfer never leaves.
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: 1/N must be computed in floating point. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Fill value written as 1/N with int N > 1: every entry is 0 and the row sums to 0.
